claude.rationale: The deal is a whole-company all-cash reverse triangular merger in which Avista's entire business — regulated utility operations, the Alaska subsidiary, and non-utility ventures — crosses into Hydro One's ownership together "with no carve-out or spin-off of any tier," so the customer-facing utility assets (T4) and their operating processes (T5) move as one intact surviving corporation (gap_45=0). Officer and management continuity, a fixed board drawing on incumbent Avista directors, a three-year employee-terms-parity commitment, and headquarters/community/safety ring-fencing show T5 processes and T6 people/organization transferring aligned coherently (gap_56=0). Because product, process, and people were bridged within the merged entity rather than separated, no structural gap exists at closing and gap_mitigated is NA. T1 is coded replace because Avista's controlling intent exits and it becomes an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Hydro One under a reconstituted board and delisting.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was structured as a whole-company cash acquisition where all of Avista's operating segments and subsidiaries would become part of the surviving corporation. The product/asset, process, and people/management tiers were bridged together without separation, meaning no structural gaps (gap_45=0, gap_56=0) were created at closing.

grok.rationale: The slice structures a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which all Avista operating segments and subsidiaries cross with no carve-out, so the customer-facing utility product (T4) and the generating/transmitting/distributing processes (T5) move together; gap_45 is therefore 0. Officers of Avista immediately before closing become officers of the surviving corporation, with board seats reserved for sitting Avista directors, a three-year employee-terms-parity commitment, and headquarters/service-quality ring-fencing, so T5 and T6 are bridged rather than separated at closing; gap_56 is 0 and gap_mitigated is NA.
